suggestions.quote: What if you saw everyone's real odds of success?
suggestions.fix: Keep this title line, then add “So... do you quit?” Move the longer fees-and-time calculation later as its answer so the chosen QUIT? thumbnail pays off immediately.

suggestions.quote: Here's how it works. Each chip is one person's chance at the one thing they'd choose... with nobody watching. It never tells you what that thing is.
suggestions.fix: Replace the final sentence with “It never tells you what that thing is. You have to watch the person.” Remove the later SECOND STALL, HIS OWN RANK and MUSIC chip labels; reveal those goals through the existing tin, exam form and keyboard instead.

suggestions.quote: > SCENE: A blink-long cut as the bus passes: the chai stall (the stall layers from before, plus a half-down shutter), the chaiwala dropping coins into a tin with a drawing of a second stall on it. His chip ticks up.
suggestions.fix: Cut this repeated explanation and move directly from the topper to Aarav's dark window. The city montage then grows toward its emotional turn instead of revisiting a reveal already completed.

keep.quote: You can't borrow someone's odds. Only their apron.
The biggest number? It tells you what's likely. It can't tell you what's worth choosing.
